definition.def: If you cannot conceive of something, you cannot imagine it or believe it.
examples: I just can't even conceive of that quantity of money. [VERB + of]
He was immensely ambitious but unable to conceive of winning power for himself. [VERB + of]

definition.def: If you conceive something as a particular thing, you consider it to be that thing.
examples: The ancients conceived the Earth as afloat in water. [VERB noun + as]
We conceive of the family as being in a constant state of change. [VERB + of]
Elvis conceived of himself as a ballad singer. [VERB + of]

definition.def: If you conceive a plan or idea, you think of it and work out how it can be done.
examples: She had conceived the idea of a series of novels. [VERB noun]
He conceived of the first truly portable computer in 1968. [VERB + of]

definition.def: When a woman conceives, she becomes pregnant.
examples: Women, he says, should give up alcohol before they plan to conceive. [VERB]
About one in six couples has difficulty conceiving. [VERB]
A mother who already has non-identical twins is more likely to conceive another set of twins. [VERB noun]

examples.sentence: It is difficult to conceive of vigorous economic growth without an efficient transport system.
Niels Bohr, the Nobel prize-winning father of modern atomic theory, jumped off from this interesting idea to conceive his now-famous model of the atom.

It must have been within the grasp of the earliest humans to conceive that four birds are distinct from two birds; however, it is not an elementary step to associate the number 4, as connected with four birds, to the number 4, as connected with four rocks.
it is impossible to conceive of a self arising outside of social experience.
At the least, these scientific advances may offer a way of screening parents who might be at risk of transmitting a single-gene defect to any children that they conceive.
